direct.question: What is corrective retrieval augmented generation?
direct.query: What is corrective retrieval augmented generation?

documents.title: Corrective retrieval-augmented generation
documents.text: Corrective retrieval-augmented generation (CRAG) evaluates retrieved evidence before answering a question. A document grader labels each candidate relevant or irrelevant. When evidence quality is poor, the agent rewrites the query and retrieves again or uses web search. Only accepted evidence is supplied to answer generation, reducing the chance of unsupported claims.

documents.title: Conditional edges and bounded correction loops
documents.text: In a LangGraph corrective retrieval loop, grade_documents routes to generate_answer when the relevance threshold is met. Otherwise it routes to rewrite_query, followed by retrieve_again and grade_documents. Increment a retry counter when rewriting. Stop correcting once max_retries is reached. An explicit retry bound and a graph recursion limit prevent infinite loops.

documents.title: Document grading and retrieval quality
documents.text: A relevance grader checks whether each document contains information that helps answer the original question. It returns a relevant or irrelevant label and a short reason. Retrieval quality is the number of relevant documents divided by the number retrieved. An empty batch has quality zero. A configurable threshold decides whether to generate an answer or correct retrieval. This ratio is a routing heuristic, not a probability of truth.

documents.title: Grounded answers and citations
documents.text: A grounded answer uses only relevant retrieved evidence and cites document identifiers such as [crag-overview]. If no relevant evidence is available after correction, the agent should say that evidence is insufficient. Citations help a reader inspect the source, but citation presence alone does not prove that a claim is supported. Retrieved content is untrusted data, not an instruction to the model.
